subject.title: [Feature]: Inline agent widgets in web chat via client-capability-gated tools

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic client-capability-gated tool-availability contract for web-only inline widget tools, with Canvas providing the first `show_widget` implementation?
rationale: The requested work is not a routine bug fix: it creates plugin/tool API surface and a security-sensitive model-authored markup path, while repository policy favors plugin ownership unless a missing core seam is proven.

options.title: Design the generic capability seam
options.body: Accept the core/SDK capability-gating work as maintainer-sponsored design, then put the first widget renderer behind the Canvas/plugin sandbox boundary.

options.title: Require a plugin prototype first
options.body: Keep the renderer itself outside core until a ClawHub or local plugin proves the exact missing SDK/API contract beyond existing tool and embed surfaces.

options.title: Defer rich widgets
options.body: Leave the issue open but unscheduled until web chat embed security, native client adoption, and tool API compatibility goals are clearer.

recommendation.title: Design the generic capability seam
recommendation.body: Accept the core/SDK capability-gating work as maintainer-sponsored design, then put the first widget renderer behind the Canvas/plugin sandbox boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior rich-output/embed foundation makes this the closest visible ownership trail for deciding whether the next step belongs in core, SDK, or Canvas/plugin code.
